text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--Foreign investement in Denmark fell to nine billion crowns in 1996 from 28 billion in 1995, the OECD says.
--Codan Bank is preparing to revise upward its forecast for Danish economic growth, saying that exports are playing a leading role in the upswing.
--Almost 30 percent of local authorities plan to cut home-help services.
--Local authorities have started a hunt for tax-dodgers.
--Danish pork producers are far from being able to meet heightened quality control demands from British retail chains, threatening exports.
--EU agricultural reform entails savings of 42 billion crowns, agriculture organisation COPA says.
--Danish company Chr.Hansen is selling advanced gene-manipulation technology abroad, but Danish food producers dare not use it for fear of adverse consumer reaction.

--The ruling Social Democrats have gained support in the EU and internationally and the spillover effect from a highly publicised visit by U.S. President Bill Clinton has strengthened them still further.
